chunks: 2460 - Bakr ibn Salih narrated from Sulaiman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him say: “Upon every nostril of a horse there is a devil. So when one of you wants to bridle it, then let him mention the Name of Allah.”

key_terms.شَيْطَانٌ: a devil; a harmful satanic presence
key_terms.فَلْيُسَمِّ: let him mention the Name of Allah
key_terms.يُلْجِمَهَا: to place a bridle on it

ai.seo_question: Why should one say Bismillah when bridling a horse?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that one should mention the Name of Allah when bridling a horse. It reflects the Islamic practice of beginning actions with remembrance of Allah as a means of protection and blessing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2460 - Bakr ibn Salih narrated from Sulaiman ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari, from Abu al-Hasan (as), who said:
"I heard him say: 'Every horse has a devil on its nostrils. So, when any of you wishes to bridle it, let them say Bismillah (In the name of Allah (swt)).'"
